content.user_title: Build Azure Blob Storage Java Apps
content.value_statement: Azure Blob Storage integration requires many Java SDK patterns for clients, uploads, downloads, and access control. This skill provides focused examples for common blob workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for the Azure Storage Blob SDK for Java.
Demonstrates service, container, and blob client creation with SAS tokens, connection strings, and DefaultAzureCredential.
Covers upload and download patterns for strings, files, streams, and output streams.
Explains listing, hierarchy traversal, copy, delete, metadata, HTTP headers, and lease operations.
Includes examples for SAS token creation, proxy configuration, and common BlobStorageException handling.
limitations: Does not create a complete application structure or build files beyond dependency guidance.
Does not validate Azure permissions, account settings, network rules, or production security policy.
Uses placeholder credentials and endpoint values that users must replace safely.
Does not cover asynchronous client patterns or every advanced Azure Storage feature.

use_cases.title: Add Blob Storage to a Java Service
use_cases.description: Use the examples to create clients and upload or download data from application workflows.

use_cases.title: Implement Storage Operations for Cloud Tools
use_cases.description: Reference listing, metadata, copy, delete, and lease patterns while building storage automation.

use_cases.title: Review Azure SDK Usage Patterns
use_cases.description: Compare existing code against standard SDK calls for authentication, streaming, SAS tokens, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Blob Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for connecting to Azure Blob Storage.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-storage-blob-java skill to show the basic Java setup for an Azure Blob Storage client. Include the dependency and a simple client creation approach.

prompt_templates.title: Add Upload and Download Logic
prompt_templates.scenario: Common application workflow for moving blob content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-storage-blob-java skill to draft Java guidance for uploading a local file and downloading a blob to a file. Use placeholder names for credentials and paths.

prompt_templates.title: Design Container Listing and Metadata Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate storage workflow with container inspection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-storage-blob-java skill to plan a Java workflow that lists blobs by prefix, reads blob properties, and updates metadata safely.

prompt_templates.title: Review Secure SAS and Proxy Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of access and networking patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-storage-blob-java skill to review a Java Azure Blob Storage design that needs SAS tokens, lease handling, proxy configuration, and error handling guidance.

output_examples.input: Need a Java upload path for an Azure Blob Storage file.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with the required SDK dependency, client type, authentication choice, upload method, overwrite behavior, and validation points.

output_examples.input: Need to list blobs under a folder-like prefix and read metadata.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step outline covering container client use, prefix filtering, hierarchy handling, property reads, and metadata update considerations.

output_examples.input: Need safer guidance for generating a read-only SAS token.
output_examples.output: A focused checklist for limited permissions, short expiration, blob or container scope, secure handling, and environment-specific testing.

best_practices: Use managed identity or DefaultAzureCredential when the deployment environment supports it.
Keep connection strings and SAS tokens out of source control and logs.
Validate overwrite, delete, lease, and SAS permissions in a nonproduction account first.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real connection strings or SAS tokens into prompts, examples, or commits.
Do not grant broad SAS permissions when read-only or short-lived access is enough.
Do not assume sample container, blob, or local file names match production naming rules.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps draft Java SDK patterns for Azure Blob Storage clients, containers, blobs, uploads, downloads, listing, metadata, leases, and SAS tokens.

faq.question: Does it include real Azure credentials?
faq.answer: No. It uses placeholders for endpoints, connection strings, SAS tokens, and account values.

faq.question: Can it replace Azure security review?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation examples, but access policy, network policy, and secret handling need environment-specific review.

faq.question: Which authentication methods are shown?
faq.answer: The skill shows SAS tokens, connection strings, and DefaultAzureCredential patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover streaming blobs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes stream upload, stream download, blob input stream, and blob output stream examples.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
